Organization 3: Ometz Agency URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/agenceometz/
Website: http://www.ometz.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5151
chemin Côte-Sainte-Catherine, Montreal QC H3W 1M6 514-342-0000 514-342-2371 Social
networks Mission JOIN OUR TEAM AND HELP TRANSFORM LIVES Agence Ometz is an
organization of charity that supports and encourages individuals and families by offering a wide

range of social, educational, employment and immigration services. Our work is guided by our
values fundamental: autonomy, inclusion, human dignity, supportive communities and excellence.
We are dedicated to helping those who seek our support to achieve their full potential and improve
their quality of life. By joining the Ometz Agency, you will work with a team of professionals who are
compassionate, committed and inspiring. Apply today! Description Building on over 150 years of

excellent community service, Agence Ometz was created in April 2008. It is the result of the merger
of Emploi Juif Montréal (JEM), Jewish Family Services (JFS) and Jewish Immigrant Assistance
Services (JIAS). The Ometz Agency offers a whole range of integrated services relating to all
stages of life. We are committed to strengthening those who are going through difficult times in their
lives. In 1863, when Montreal had just under 1,000 Jews, a group of leaders communities met in a

store on rue Saint-Jacques and created the Young Men’s Hebrew Benevolent Society. They were
then far from suspecting that they were founding what would later become Jewish Family Services
(JFS). The growing wave of immigrants to Canada, partly due to the many newcomers fleeing their
country and who risked being deported upon their arrival, justified the creation of Assistance
Services for Jewish Immigrants (JIAS) in 1922. Over the years, JIAS has helped hundreds of

thousands of Jewish immigrants in their immigration application procedures and to settle in
Canada. In 1945, Jewish Employment Montreal (JEM) was founded to meet the needs of Canadian
veterans war and people arriving from Europe in search of work. By the variety of services offered
to job seekers and employers, JEM has become a Montreal leader in employment and placement
matters. Currently, there are more than 13,000 people per year who contact the Ometz Agency with

the aim of improving their quality of life. The Agency offers a set of services for the whole family
whether it concerns difficulties experienced following the breakdown of family or mental illness,
financial issues, looking for a job or installation in Montreal.

consultation: We work with the partners of the community to better meet the needs of immigrant
families

Organization 5: Côte-des-Neiges job search center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centrederecherchedemploicotedesneiges/ Website:

Montreal QC H3S 1K5 514-733-3026 514-733-7120 Social networks Contacts (1) AMAL OBAID
Director 514-733-3026 extension: 216 Communicate with this contact Mission Make available to

participants all information resources necessary to find and obtain a job corresponding to their
qualifications and their aspirations as quickly as possible, as well as promoting individual
responsibility in job search. Description Group sessions Job Search Club Three-week sessions on
job search techniques according to the Job Search Club method. This method is used successfully
in Quebec for almost twenty years. We offer you: Dynamic three-week sessions where you contact

employers, land interviews, improve your resume, find job prospects in a positive and stimulating
group atmosphere; Of professional advisors; A simulated video interview; A documentation center;
A fax and photocopy service, computers and Internet access; A three-month follow-up. Admission
criteria: Be aged 18 and over Be available to carry out a search of full-time employment Have a
clear and realistic employment objective Live on the Island of Montreal To to participate in a Job

Search Club session you must first attend a session information Individual services Resume writing
The Job Search Center Côte-des-Neiges offers you help in writing your resume and your cover
letter. presentation in French or English. To make an appointment call: 514-733-302 Employment
counseling for manual workers Employment counseling offered individually for people looking for
manual work. Admission criteria: Be newly arrived in Canada (less than 5 years old) or be a person

who is part of visible minorities Be aged 18 years and over Hold a Sec diploma. V or less Speak
French or English For information and registration: 514-733-3026 Employment counseling for
newcomers Employment counseling offered on an individual basis Admission criteria: Be a new
arrival in Canada ( priority given to people residing in Canada for 6 months or less) Be 18 years old
and more Hold a college or university diploma For information and registration: 514-733-3026

Organization 6: Parents involved in early childhood - PEP URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/hippyquebec/ Website:
http://www.parentsengages.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Head office 5964
avenue Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, bureau 206, Montréal QC H4A 1N1 5144841471, ext. 230 Opening
hours SCHEDULE From Monday to Friday by appointment. Flexible, according to the schedules
defined between the speakers at home and parents. Social networks Contacts (1) MARIE-JOSÉE

PERREAULT Director general 5144841471 extension: 230 Communicate with this contact Mission
Parents committed to early childhood has the mission of offering, developing and supporting,
particularly in Quebec, primarily home-based programs aimed at improving the aptitude of
immigrant parents and from disadvantaged backgrounds to strengthen their children's ability to
learn at a young age as well as than to better prepare them for school. Description Program

Activities are offered at each visit, to families' homes, 30 weeks per year by home workers. Home
visits are made every week or every two weeks, depending on the needs of the parents. The
activities, both fun and educational, are focused on the development overall health of the child.
Parents become familiar with the observation and development of skills through play and daily
activities at home. The speaker brings a new book in the family, so that parent and child enjoy

exploring a diversity of books and establish a reading routine at home. Thus, the parent is made
aware of the importance of exposing your child to reading to support them in their language
development in particular. The targeted skills work on language, the development of fine motor
skills and overall, memory and listening skills, as well as emotional development and coordination
oculo-manual. Additionally, parents can discuss parenting techniques with the speaker and we also

do SEO. Group activities Group activities group on different subjects and outings are organized for
parents.

Organization 7: ACAT Canada URL: https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/acatcanada/
Website: http://acatcanada.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details Chemin
de la Côte-Sainte-Catherine, Montreal QC H3T1B6 514-890-6169 Social networks Mission
Christian Action for the abolition of torture (ACAT) is the Canadian branch of an international
federation, FIACAT, having consultative status at the UN. ACAT Canada is a national ecumenical

organization that has been defending human rights for nearly 40 years. It intervenes especially in
cases torture and the death penalty. It informs through awareness and action campaigns,
intervenes through letters of protest from its members to the authorities concerned, educates to
human rights, invites spiritual reflection and above all, ensures that situations are reported to the
UN of mistreatment still existing in Canada. Its head office is in Montreal and its activities are take

place in French, but it has members across Canada. Description Pleas, Human rights education,
Spirituality, Support for healing victims of torture

Organization 9: Jamaican Association of Montreal URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/associationjamaicainedemontreal/ Website: None
Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 4065, rue Jean-Talon Ouest, Montréal
QC H4P 1W6 514 737-8229 Mission Welcome, support and integrate new arrivals Jamaicans and
members of cultural communities in Montreal. We offer resources, activities and a support network

to promote their integration and development in our community. Description The Jamaican
Association of Montreal is a community organization committed to providing essential support to
members of the Jamaican community residing in Montreal. Our mission is to promote the
integration and development of Jamaicans and Newly arrived Jamaicans, as well as other cultural
communities in the region. The Jamaican Association of Montreal intervenes mainly in the areas of

cultural communities and newcomers, offering a range of services specifically adapted to the needs
of these diverse populations. Our dedicated team works closely collaboration with community
members to support them in their journey installation and integration in Montreal. We offer activities,
workshops and programs aimed at promoting cultural diversity, solidarity and social inclusion.
Furthermore, we regularly organize festive and cultural events to celebrate the wealth and vitality of

Jamaican culture and other communities present in our city. Join the Jamaican Association of
Montreal to benefit from warm support and a network united. Together, let's build a strong and
dynamic community in Montreal!

Organization 10: Baobab Family URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/baobabfamilial/ Website:
http://www.baobabfamilial.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Head office 599-6767
ch. Côte-des-Neiges, Montreal QC H3S 2T6 514-734-4097 Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday 1
p.m. to 6 p.m. Tuesday 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. and 1 p.m. – 6 p.m. Wednesday 9 a.m. – 12 p.m. and 1
p.m. – 6 p.m. Thursday 9 a.m. – 12 p.m. and 1 p.m. – 6 p.m. Social networks Mission Le Baobab

Familial is a family home, a living environment, a gathering place that promotes mutual aid,
exchange and the feeling of belonging to one's environment. We welcome and support families by
enriching their family and community life. Our work is oriented towards families in a spirit of respect,
integrity and collaboration. Description The Family Baobab offers various services intended for
families in the Côte-des-neiges district: Welcome, listening, referral and support; homework help;

community daycare; respite at home;; teen group; sports activities for women and girls; activities for
fathers; sharing cafes and thematic workshops; workshops on the rights and responsibilities of
children, on the migratory journey and on parenting skills; etc. The Baobab Familial also offers all
kinds of activities social and cultural character. Our outings allow our families to discover Quebec
(beach, apples, sugar shacks, etc.), collective kitchens and community suppers are as much
opportunity to meet and share.

Organization 11: Multi-LISTENING listening and reference center URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centredecouteetdereferencemultiecoute/ Website:
http://www.multiecoute.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 3600
Avenue Barclay, Montréal QC H3S 1K5 514-737-3604 Hours SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 9:00
a.m. to 5:00 p.m. However, our active listening and monitoring services will always be 24/7 during

the end of the year. weeks as well as holidays at this number: (514) 378 – 3430 Social networks
Mission La The mission of the Multi-LISTENING Center is to provide mental health prevention and
help the social integration of anyone who feels the need; we pay attention particular to immigrants.
Services offered: telephone listening in several languages, psychosocial follow-ups, filling out forms
(citizenship, work permits and others), oath. Description The Multi-LISTENING CENTER is a

listening and help center psychosocial and reference for the individual. It offers its services while
respecting the culture of participant and, wherever possible, in the client’s original language. In this
sense, the Multi-Audition pays particular attention to immigrants. The Multi-Listening Center aims
to: Come helping anyone in need. Offer active listening to people who have need for help, to talk, to

confide, to support, that is to say getting the participant to verbalize his feelings and needs so that
he feels understood. Undertake psychosocial follow-up short and medium term with participants
who wish to set goals and work towards improving their well-being and living conditions. Inform and
refer participants to local resources to improve the steps taken at the Center. Helping immigrants
and newcomers to adapt and better integrate into the host society. Bring the person to find within

her the resources and solutions to her problems, and if necessary, help her find the external
resources that can meet their needs.

Organization 15: Center for Immigrant Workers - IWC CTI URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/centredestravailleursettravailleusesimmigrants/
Website: http://www.iwc-cti.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 4755,
Avenue Van Horne, Montréal QC H3W 1H8 514-342-2111 514-227-2268 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Monday 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. Tuesday 1:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Wednesday 1:00 p.m.

to 5:00 p.m. Thursday 1:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Social networks Mission Le Center for Immigrant
Workers (CTI) defends the rights of immigrants in their workplaces and fights for dignity, respect
and justice. Some of our goals The main ones are: (cid:127) Promote popular education,
particularly with regard to the rights of workers (cid:127) Improving working conditions for workers
and immigrant workers (cid:127) Organize mobilization around problems related to conditions work,

including for example: accidents at work, harassment, unpaid wages, overtime, maternity leave,
etc. (cid:127) Provide a space that allows workers and immigrant workers to receive information,
resources, and references. We offer these resources and references in several languages (English,
French, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Iranian, Bengali, etc.) Join us to know your rights, acquire the tools
that will allow you to improve your conditions at work, and to promote a movement for economic

and social justice. Description Information and references on labor rights. Course on rights and
unionism for workers. Basic training on computer. Organization of cultural and social events such
as Mai l’oeuvre! Montreal and International Women's Day.

Organization 18: Hellenic Community of Greater Montreal - CHGM URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/communautehelleniquedugrandmontreal/ Website:
http://www.hcgm.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5757, avenue
Wilderton, Montréal QC H3S 2K8 514-738-2421 514-738-5466 Opening hours SCHEDULE
Branches (5) CENTER COMMUNITY AND SPORTS 5757, avenue Wilderton 514-738-2421
514-738-5466 CENTER COMMUNITY AND SPORTS SOUTH SHORE 5220, Grande Allée

450-656-4832 450-656-1531 BUREAU LAVAL 450-688-2088 450-688-2084 LAVAL SPORTS
CENTER 450-681-5952 450-688-1834 HEAD OFFICE 5777, ave Wilderton 514-738-2421
514-738-5466 Mission La Hellenic Community of Greater Montreal serves the Greek population of
the greater region of Montreal (Montreal, Laval and South Shore) since 1906. For more than 100
years, the CHGM has never stopped representing the proud citizens of Quebec of Greek origin,

who settled and continue to settle in the greater Montreal area. The CHGM provides the population
of Greek origin a variety of services: (cid:127) Education (cid:127) Church (cid:127) Culture
(cid:127) Social (cid:127) Sport (cid:127) Volunteering (cid:127) Member services (cid:127) And
much more Our goal is to constantly enrich and unify members of our community, by bringing them
together, meeting their needs and strengthening our ties with other cultural communities in the

Greater Montreal region. Our ancestors built their dream, we preserve our heritage for generations
to come! Description The goals of the Community are to ensure the flourishing of the culture of
population of Greek origin in the Montreal region and in particular: (cid:127) to preserve and
promote the Greek language; (cid:127) to set up works of charity, well-being and education for the
benefit of the population of Greek origin; (cid:127) to preserve and perpetuate the Greek Orthodox

faith and the tradition promulgated by the authority of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of
Constantinople, following the doctrine and faith proclaimed and applied by the Greek Orthodox
Church, and according to ecclesiastical authority and the religious rules designated by this
patriarchy.

Organization 19: Moldovan Community of Quebec URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/communaute-moldave-du-quebec/ Website:
https://www.moldovaquebec.ca/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 6767
chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, bureau 693-5, Montréal QC H3S 2T6 438 937-3608 514 351-7949
Opening hours SCHEDULE 4th Thursday of each month Mission The mission of the Moldavian
Community of Quebec is to unite and to support the Moldovan diaspora through cultural, social and

educational activities. We aim to strengthen ties between community members and promote culture
Moldovan in Quebec. Description Moldovan Community of Quebec The Moldovan Community of
Quebec is an organization dedicated to bringing together Moldovans living in Quebec and
promoting their culture and their traditions. Founded by Ala Mindicanu, the president of the
community, the organization offers various events and activities to strengthen ties within the

Moldovan diaspora. Mission and Objectives The mission of the Moldovan Community of Quebec is
to promote Moldovan culture, to offer a space for exchange and support to members of the
community, and to promote the integration of Moldovans in Quebec. Among its objectives are the
establishment of intergenerational projects and the consolidation of links with the homeland of
origin. Events and Activities The organization regularly organizes cultural events, meetings and

conferences to celebrate Moldovan culture and encourage exchanges between members. Of Legal
consultations are also offered to help Moldovans in their procedures administrative. Consular
Services The Moldovan Community of Quebec offers services consular services to members of the
Moldovan community. These services include the realization specific notarial acts and other
administrative procedures. It is recommended to take make an appointment in advance to benefit

from these services. Partnerships and Collaborations The organization collaborates with the
Romanian Cultural Association (ACR) to implement projects intergenerational and promote the
culture of the region. The Moldovan Community of Quebec is also involved in initiatives to
strengthen ties with Moldova. Contact For more information on the Moldovan Community of
Quebec and its activities, you can visit their website at www.moldovaquebec.ca or contact them by
phone at 613-695-6168.

Organization 20: Unified Sephardic Community of Quebec - CSUQ URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/communautesefaradeunifieeduquebec/ Website:
http://www.csuq.org/ Description: ABOUT THE ORGANIZATION Contact details 5151 Chemin De
la Côte-Sainte-Catherine, Montreal QC 514-733-4998, ext. 3120 514-739-8366 Opening hours
SCHEDULE Our offices are open Monday to Thursday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Friday from 8 a.m.

to 2 p.m. Mission Preserve, enrich, and promote Sephardic culture and identity. Description Part
stakeholder of a multi-ethnic society and an open door to today’s Quebec, the CSUQ aims to assert
itself as the vector of a plural Jewish culture, capable of contributing to the enrichment of our
metropolis through the production of high-level activities in the Arts and Letters. The CSUQ thus
has several cultural groups, including a musical ensemble – “La Chorale Kinor” –, an association

promoting the traditional Sephardic liturgy – The Association of Sephardic Hazanim and Paytanim
of Canada, and an art gallery – Galeria – allowing the promotion of Sephardic artists. Montrealers
have learned for years to discover and appreciate the Sephardic contribution through the Sephardic
Festival. This prestigious event allows them, each summer, to familiarize themselves with the
richness of one culture at the same time traditional and contemporary which is now part of Quebec

and Canadian heritage. A committee of French-speaking Jewish Women also works for the
recognition of an identity Sephardic women within Canada.

Organization 21: Vietnamese Community in Canada – Montreal Region URL:
https://macommunaute.ca/bottin-des-agences/communaute-vietnamienne-au-canada-regi
on-montreal/ Website: https://communautevietmontreal.com/ Description: ABOUT THE
ORGANIZATION Contact details 6767 chemin de la Côte-des-Neiges, bureau 495, Montréal QC
H3S 2T6 514 340-9630 514 340-1926 Opening hours SCHEDULE Monday to Friday 9:00 a.m. to
12:00 p.m. and 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. Mission Accompany and support the Vietnamese newly

settled in Canada, women, children and victims of domestic violence. We offer support, translation
and assistance services administrative and social support to promote their integration into
Canadian society. Description The Vietnamese Community in Canada – Montreal Region is an
organization of non-profit charity that provides support to diverse groups of people in need.
Founded in 1976, the organization has evolved to become a multi-service agency always focused

on volunteering and helping Vietnamese newcomers to Canada. Following the arrival of a first
group of Vietnamese refugees in Canada in 1975, the Vietnamese diaspora quickly developed,
concentrated mainly in the province of Quebec, particularly in Montreal. The Services offered by the
Vietnamese Community in Canada – Montreal Region include: Accompaniment to medical
appointments and meetings with managers government Translation of documents and

correspondence, interpretation during meetings Official help with filling out forms Support for
women and children victims of violence In addition to these services, the organization offers
French, computer and cooking courses. to facilitate the integration of newcomers into Canadian
society. The Community Vietnamese in Canada – Montreal region played an active role during the
COVID-19 pandemic Covid-19, providing mental and physical support to the elderly, single and

sick. The organization also participated in Covid-19 vaccination and aid initiatives for homeless.
The close bond with the Vietnamese community is a fundamental value of the organization, which
strives to maintain this commitment through various events and celebrations, such as Tigris Tet and
community excursions. The Community Vietnamese in Canada – Montreal region is an essential
